tagline: Trusted to transform missions with the power of tomorrow's technologies.
hero_kpi_rationale: Booz Allen's total revenue increased 12% to approximately $12.4 billion in fiscal 2025, reflecting strong demand for its advanced technology solutions in AI, cybersecurity, and cloud for critical U.S. government missions.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total amount of revenue generated by the company during the fiscal year.
kpis.description: Revenue increased 12% in fiscal 2025, driven by strong demand for solutions and services, headcount growth, and billable expenses.
kpis.signal: Sustained revenue growth driven by demand.

kpis.name: Reduction in Provision for Claimed Costs
kpis.explanation: Reduction recorded in the provision for historical costs claimed to the government following audits.
kpis.description: A $122 million reduction in the provision for claimed costs was recorded in the second quarter of fiscal 2025, compared to $18 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2024.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Percentage of revenue remaining after deducting operating costs.
kpis.description: Operating margin improved to 11% in fiscal 2025 from 10% in fiscal 2024, reflecting improved efficiency, cost management, and insurance recoveries.

kpis.name: Operating Income
kpis.explanation: Amount of profit generated from operations before interest and taxes.
kpis.description: Operating income increased 35% to $1,370 million in fiscal 2025 from $1,014 million in fiscal 2024, driven by the same revenue growth drivers and cost management efforts.

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees working for the company.
kpis.description: Total headcount of approximately 35,800 employees increased to support business growth and meet rising client demand for advanced technology solutions.
kpis.signal: Headcount growth to meet increasing demand.

risks.title: Government Audit Impacting Results
risks.score_rationale: The risk is listed first in the 10-K and describes a material impact on revenue, operating income, and earnings per share. The language is repeated and emphasizes the materiality and uncertainty of future adjustments based on ongoing audits. The Regulation category is highly weighted for government contracting firms. This risk is stable compared to the prior year.

risks.title: Critical Estimates in Revenue Recognition
risks.score_rationale: The risk is classified as a critical accounting estimate, with emphasis on uncertainty in EAC (Estimate-at-Completion) and variable revenue. The text highlights that estimation changes could significantly impact contract profitability. Although recurring, the intensity of language and potential impact justify high severity. Accounting category is heavily weighted.

risks.title: Provision for Disputed Claimed Costs
risks.score_rationale: This risk is explicitly linked to accounting provisions for future adjustments on historical costs since 2011. It is cited as potentially having a material impact on earnings. The direct link to potential losses and the continuity of government audits reinforce its existential nature. Identical to audit risk but distinct in text.

risks.title: Uncertain Tax Positions and Reserves
risks.score_rationale: The text describes significant judgments required for taxes, reserves for uncertain tax positions, and potential impact on the effective tax rate. Tax regulatory uncertainty is high, particularly with past judicial decisions (DC OTR). The risk is stable but with ongoing exposure.

risks.title: Ability to Generate Future Revenues for Deferred Tax Assets
risks.score_rationale: The portfolio of deferred tax assets depends on the generation of future profits. If the company does not generate sufficient taxable income, a valuation allowance must be recorded. This would directly impact net income. The risk is recurring, with cautious language but no indication of worsening or improvement.

risks.title: Centralized Management of Single Segment
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in a single segment, limiting diversification of operational and financial risks. While this promotes collaboration, it increases vulnerability to sector-wide or customer-specific shocks. The language is neutral, but the lack of segmentation is a structural risk concentration factor.
